target_customer: Immigrants without US credit history (students, H1B holders, DACA recipients), later fintechs and neobanks needing credit infrastructure (Onbo)
problem: Newcomers to the US cannot get loans or credit because they lack a US credit history, even when they have stable incomes.
business_model: Consumer loans funded by debt facilities, later B2B credit-as-a-service API

founders.name: Rohit Mittal
founders.background_notes: Data scientist at PopSugar per TechCrunch May 2020. YC page says he raised 350M dollars in debt. Became SVP and GM of Lending at JG Wentworth after the sale.

founders.name: Priyank Singh
founders.background_notes: Software developer at A9 and Microsoft per TechCrunch May 2020. YC page lists him as CTO and co-founder of Helium Ventures.

exit.reason: Platform and related assets sold, announced 2022-12-05; terms undisclosed

technical_complexity.rationale: Underwriting without US credit files and building loan servicing took real engineering, but used standard fintech components.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary credit data on immigrants and debt facility relationships helped, but the lending model was replicable by banks and fintechs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it early on; JG Wentworth bought the platform in December 2022 to enter consumer lending.

market_need_then: Immigrants searching for loans such as H1B loans had few options; the founders themselves were immigrants (Singh came as a student per trade press). Dated 2016 demand figures were not found.

rebrands.to: Onbo (B2B credit product brand launched alongside Stilt)
rebrands.why: Expansion from consumer loans to B2B credit infrastructure, per PR Newswire headline

branding.community_and_virality: People reportedly find Stilt by searching terms like H1B loan (American Banker).

brand_strength.rationale: Niche brand with search-driven discovery; no source shows mascot, community or press about the brand itself.

pivots.why: Launched Onbo to let companies offer credit without a bank sponsor

outcome_analysis: Stilt started in YC Winter 2016 offering loans to immigrants lacking US credit history, funded mostly by debt facilities after a 7.5M dollar seed in May 2020 and a 100M SVB facility in January 2021. In March 2022 it announced 114M in debt and equity and launched Onbo. JG Wentworth bought the lending platform in December 2022 for an undisclosed price, which looks like an asset sale rather than a venture exit, and the lending program was later reported on hold in an undated consumer guide.
notes: Company site stilt.com returned HTTP 403, not fetched. Round list stops at 2022 and the earlier years are not covered. PYMNTS labels the March 2022 round as 14M dollars Series A while TechCrunch and PR Newswire say 114M in debt and equity; the stage is recorded as other because sources conflict. JG Wentworth said Stilt raised 322M in debt and equity in total. Education of founders not found. Stilt is described as an asset and platform sale, so exit type acquisition is a simplification.
